title: The Natty FREAK with Superhero Aesthetics (Bald Omni-Man)
summary: A lifter profile of Paris Butler (Bald Omni-Man). NH reviews his flexible Berserk Method five-day full-body split run over 10-11 days, then praises his mix of biomechanics knowledge and heavy, big-mover training, his use of isolation, and his slow lean bulk. He grades the physique muscle by muscle, explaining how long limbs and a short torso shaped his strengths and weak points. Opens by thanking viewers: Ko-fi memberships secured the channel in under 10 hours.
claims: Ko-fi memberships reached the goal within 10 hours, so YouTube becomes his paid second job with no ads or sponsors
A good program is flexible; if dropping one exercise or rep range breaks it, it's a bad program
Bald Omni-Man runs five training days within a 10-11 day window, taking rest days when needed rather than on fixed days
Floating rest days are for advanced lifters; novices need fixed structure such as Mon/Wed/Fri
On a full-body day, start with legs because they are the most taxing and you are freshest
Leg press before a heel-elevated SSB squat 'pre-ignites' the quads for lifters with long legs who can't reach quad failure on squats
Two compound leg movements is enough for a full-body day
You don't have to hit every muscle on a 'full body' day; following split names to the letter is a mistake, just hit what needs hitting over the week
He prefers to stay below 12 reps on compound movements
Push the leg press hard in moderate reps; don't do 30-rep sets
An arm or isolation day mid-week replaces a rest day with low-fatigue volume without hurting recovery; true full rest days should become rare as you advance
Heavy pulls from the floor like RDLs need few sets; most people can only do them hard once a week, and sets of 20-30 waste volume
He approaches training by asking what needs hitting each day rather than following a fixed body-part schedule
Knowing biomechanics doesn't make good advice without training intensity; you need both brains and effort
Paralysis by analysis is everywhere; doing is everything, get the stimulus first
Low-bar squats let you lift more due to leverage, not more muscle work: more fatigue, less stimulus for bodybuilding
Pushing the bar away from the shins on RDLs means less weight but more hamstring and less fatigue, useful for strong lifters
Isolation is as important as compounds; moving less weight on curls doesn't mean less stimulus
Trying to get as strong as possible on every movement for every muscle with proper form is bodybuilding
Eat to fuel progression in the gym, not to gain weight; a surplus only builds muscle if your lifts and volume go up
Gaining 20 lb over three years beats 20 lb in one year: it's mostly muscle and avoids yo-yo dieting
Bulks only succeed if they are slow; that is the key to breaking the natural limit
Bald Omni-Man used to be obese
Long legs and a short torso make quads hard to grow because the hips shoot up in the squat; that is anatomy, not bad form
Genetics you're born with matter less than what you do with them; many would call his proportions bad genetics yet people think he's on drugs
Long arms give huge potential for triceps and forearm size; a natural 20-inch arm is possible for him, mostly through hard isolation
You can have capped 3D delts naturally, just without the pumped look of enhanced lifters
Long arms mean more range of motion on bench, which stretches and grows the shoulders; short-armed lifters like NH need vertical pressing for delts
Bald Omni-Man benches four plates and does about 4x8-10 with three plates
Pulling from the floor gives a passive stretch for big traps; upright rows are also a great trap and shoulder builder
Lifters' best body parts match the lifts they love and are strong at
Big lats come from heavy weighted pull-ups, chin-ups and neutral-grip pull-ups, not light pulldowns; strong-backed lifters all swear by pull-ups
Abs grow from heavy, progressively overloaded isolation done almost daily
Most people train calves poorly, which is why calves stay small
exercises: compound after leg press for long-legged lifters
Pec fly superset with adductor machine
adductors for leg size and health
